definitions.gloss: teacher (official job title, kindergarten through high school)
definitions.explanation: The legal job title of a fully licensed, regularly employed teacher at a Japanese school below university level. It appears in personnel records, news reports, and formal introductions rather than in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{中学校|ちゅうがっこう}の{教諭|きょうゆ}だ。
examples.english: My father is a junior high school teacher.

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}から{小学校|しょうがっこう}{教諭|きょうゆ}として{働|はたら}く。
examples.english: From next year I'll be working as an elementary school teacher.

examples.japanese: {市内|しない}の{高校|こうこう}に{勤|つと}める{教諭|きょうゆ}が、{優|すぐ}れた{授業|じゅぎょう}で{表彰|ひょうしょう}された。
examples.english: A teacher working at a high school in the city was honoured for the quality of his lessons.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小学校|しょうがっこう}{教諭|きょうゆ}: elementary school teacher
- {養護|ようご}{教諭|きょうゆ}: school nurse-teacher
- {教諭|きょうゆ}{免許|めんきょ}: teaching licence
- {教諭|きょうゆ}になる: to become a licensed teacher

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先生|せんせい}: teacher — how you actually address or refer to one; never a job title on paper
- {教師|きょうし}: teacher — the general occupational word, usable of any school and of private tutors
- {講師|こうし}: lecturer, part-time instructor — a different employment category from {教諭|きょうゆ}

Register note: news stories append it directly to a surname, as in {山田|やまだ}{教諭|きょうゆ}, the way English reports say "Ms Smith, a teacher at…".
